newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan says average age of U.N. staff too high.
newsitem.headline: Annan says average age of U.N. staff too high.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Thursday the average age of U.N. professional staff at 49 was too old and he wanted to bring in a younger team without firing current employees.
Admitting he was "no spring chicken" himself at the age of 59, Annan said only about 5 percent of current U.N. staff was under 35 years of age and this was an unhealthy situation.

"It may not be obvious, and you may not notice it, but we are an ageing organisation. And the average age of a U.N. professional is 49. It is far too high," he told U.N. employees at a briefing on a package of wide-ranging reforms he announced to the General Assembly on Wednesday..
Annan said nearly half the U.N. staff would retire in the next decade. "As you know, I have already pledged to eliminate 1,000 staff posts, and this will be achieved through attrition."

Asked by a staff member whether he wanted only 25- to 26-year-olds working at the United Nations, he said the age-spread in any organisation should be balanced and the percentage of under-35-year olds should be increased.

"I would be happy to see about 25, 30, or even 40 percent in that age-bracket, so that you can renew the organisation," he said. "If we do not try to promote younger people to the senior levels, we are going to have a serious problem when all the senior people retire."
He added: "I wasn't trying to cast aspersions on any age group. I myself am no spring chicken."
